item.title: GovBrief Today #659
item.description: Government lawyers admitted in a court filing today that the United States deported an American citizen, then asked the judge to throw out the man’s lawsuit. Brian José Morales García was born in Denver. In April a Texas state trooper stopped the pickup he was riding in near Fredericksburg, and he said his birth certificate and Social Security card were at home in Austin. The trooper called immigration agents. After Morales García was deported to Mexico, Customs and Border Protection said, “CBP did NOT arrest a U.S. citizen.” He was kept out of his own country for four months. In the same filing that calls Morales García a citizen, the government says it cannot be sued for what it did to him. It tried a version of this last year after admitting it sent Kilmar Abrego Garcia to El Salvador by mistake, when it told a judge she had no power to order him brought back. Abrego Garcia had a court order protecting him from that deportation, and Morales García has a Colorado birth certificate. On February 1, 2025, I typed a list of nine things I never imagined a government doing in one day and sent it to my family. I’ve sent one every night since: 10,043 stories over 659 straight nights, free and without ads. Add your email address at the website and I’ll send it to you too. NEW: Zoom In is now live! item.description: A Retro Phone Without Internet or Social Media Japanese telecommunications company KDDI introduced the INFOBAR ZERO on November 18, 2026, bringing back a classic mobile phone without modern smartphone distractions. The device removes internet browsing and social media, focusing on basic communication. It is scheduled to launch in Japan on December 25. Inspired by the original INFOBAR released in 2003, the phone features colorful rectangular buttons and a retro appearance. Its functions include voice calls, text messaging, a 2-megapixel camera, offline music playback. Users also get a calendar, alarm, calculator, although applications remain unavailable. The INFOBAR ZERO costs ¥32,780, approximately $205, with preorders already available through Japanese retailers. It comes in three color options and features a compact 2.4-inch display. KDDI designed the device for people who want to reduce their screen time without completely giving up mobile communication.
